claims.excerpt: GRACE Follow-On tracks changes in Earth’s water by measuring the changing distance between two satellites.
claims.claim: GRACE Follow-On uses changes in the distance between its satellites to help track changes in Earth’s water.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The changing inter-satellite distance is a raw measurement used to infer shifts in mass. The mission follows changes involving groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, ice sheets and changes in sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.narrative: Explain how GRACE Follow-On’s two satellites use changes in the distance between them to help investigate water movement on Earth.
claims.explanation: The piece summarizes the source’s indirect chain: distance measurements are used to infer mass shifts associated with changes in water stores.
claims.materiality: The indirect inference is preserved in the following sentences, so the summary is not misleading.

claims.excerpt: The pair follows one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart.

claims.evidence: Twin satellites follow each other about 137 miles or 220 kilometers apart.
claims.narrative: GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart.
claims.explanation: The distance and converted units match the source.
